findings.title: Merged PR comment rendering calls a helper that is not on the workflow
findings.body: `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow` (and the equivalent GitLab workflow) invokes `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)`, but the new helper was added to `CommitContextIntegration`, not to `PRCommentWorkflow`/its subclasses. Moreover, that helper calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title`, although `_truncate_title` was also added only to `CommitContextIntegration`. Generating a merged-PR suspect-issue comment will therefore raise `AttributeError` rather than posting or updating the comment. Move both helpers to the workflow base class, or invoke them through the integration consistently.

findings.title: Feature-flagged dashboard tables discard the query result
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, this branch renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and a hard-coded empty `tableData` object instead of the current `result.data` and `result.meta`. Consequently every table widget for organizations with this flag enabled renders an empty table, including after successful queries. Adapt the widget result into the visualization props rather than passing placeholder data.

findings.title: Age and timestamp exclusivity can be bypassed with zero values
findings.body: The mutual-exclusion validators test `self.initial_data.get(...)`, which treats valid integer value `0` as absent. A report containing both `age: 0` and `timestamp: 0` passes validation even though the endpoint explicitly requires the two format-specific fields not to coexist. Check key presence (for example, `'age' in self.initial_data`) rather than truthiness in both validators.

findings.title: Attribute-key query cache is no longer partitioned by organization
findings.body: The new React Query key contains only the filter-derived `queryOptions`; unlike the previous `useApiQuery` key, it does not include the organization slug. With the common all-project selection (an empty project list), navigating from one organization to another with the same date range and item/type reuses the prior organization's cached attribute collection, which is also retained while the new request is fetching via `usePrevious`. This displays cross-organization metadata and incorrect suggestions. Include `organization.slug` in the query key.

findings.title: Falsy custom cell output incorrectly triggers the default renderer
findings.body: The public renderer contract uses `undefined` to request fallback rendering, but this code tests `if (cell)`. Valid React nodes such as `0`, an empty string, `false`, or `null` are therefore ignored and replaced by the default cell/header renderer. Test specifically for `cell !== undefined` in both the body and header renderer paths so custom renderers can intentionally render falsy values or suppress a cell.
